\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فرع} (farʿ)}{فرع (farʿ)}]{\ar{فرع} (farʿ) — a branch office; a branch}

\label{lesson:AR-C452-far}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to check over, then the Arabic for to ban.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فرع}}
\textbf{\ar{فرع}} — \emph{farʿ} — \textquotedblleft{}a branch office; a branch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{فتح} \ar{البنك} \ar{فرعا} \ar{جديدا} \ar{في} \ar{حينا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fataḥa al-bank farʿan jadīdan fī ḥayyinā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bank opened a new branch in our neighbourhood.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{فروع}, \emph{furūʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فرع}} (\emph{farʿ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-r-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}a branch of a tree\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{farʿ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{farʿ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fataḥa al-bank farʿan jadīdan fī ḥayyinā.} — The bank opened a new branch in our neighbourhood.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to check over, then the Arabic for to ban, then say \emph{farʿ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فرع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A branch office; a branch\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رصيد} (raṣīd)}{رصيد (raṣīd)}]{\ar{رصيد} (raṣīd) — a balance (of an account); credit}

\label{lesson:AR-C452-rasid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to ban, then the Arabic for a branch office.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رصيد}}
\textbf{\ar{رصيد}} — \emph{raṣīd} — \textquotedblleft{}a balance (of an account); credit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{رصيد} \ar{حسابي} \ar{صغيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna raṣīd ḥisābī ṣaghīran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The balance of my account was small.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رصيد}} (\emph{raṣīd}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-ṣ-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to watch for; to make ready\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حوالة} (ḥawāla)}{حوالة (ḥawāla)}]{\ar{حوالة} (ḥawāla) — a money transfer}

\label{lesson:AR-C452-hawala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a branch office, then the Arabic for a balance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حوالة}}
\textbf{\ar{حوالة}} — \emph{ḥawāla} — \textquotedblleft{}a money transfer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أرسلت} \ar{حوالة} \ar{إلى} \ar{أختي} \ar{في} \ar{الخارج}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{arsaltu ḥawāla ilā ukhtī fī al-khārij.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I sent a money transfer to my sister abroad.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حوالة}} (\emph{ḥawāla}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-w-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to change, to shift\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{ḥawāla} shifts a sum from one hand to another.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥawāla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arsaltu ḥawāla ilā ukhtī fī al-khārij.} — I sent a money transfer to my sister abroad.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a branch office, then the Arabic for a balance, then say \emph{ḥawāla} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صرف} (ṣarafa)}{صرف (ṣarafa)}]{\ar{صرف} (ṣarafa) — to change money; to spend}

\label{lesson:AR-C452-sarafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a balance, then the Arabic for a money transfer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صرف}}
\textbf{\ar{صرف}} — \emph{ṣarafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to change money; to spend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{صرفت} \ar{مالا} \ar{في} \ar{المطار}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṣaraftu mālan fī al-maṭār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I changed money at the airport.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصرف}, \emph{yaṣrif}.

\emph{siʿr aṣ-ṣarf} is the exchange rate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صرف}} (\emph{ṣarafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-r-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to turn away, to change\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the root of \emph{ṣarrāf}, \textquotedblleft{}a money changer\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣarafa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaraftu mālan fī al-maṭār.} — I changed money at the airport.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a balance, then the Arabic for a money transfer, then say \emph{ṣarafa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أودع} (awdaʿa)}{أودع (awdaʿa)}]{\ar{أودع} (awdaʿa) — to deposit}

\label{lesson:AR-C452-awdaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a money transfer, then the Arabic for to change money.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أودع}}
\textbf{\ar{أودع}} — \emph{awdaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to deposit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أودع} \ar{أبي} \ar{المال} \ar{في} \ar{البنك}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{awdaʿa abī al-māl fī al-bank.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father deposited the money in the bank.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يودع}, \emph{yūdiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أودع}} (\emph{awdaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-d-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to leave, to let rest\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to leave a thing in someone's keeping\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}
